questions.explanation: The vaccine works before any illness exists: it builds immunity in a healthy provider so hepatitis B never takes hold, which means acting to keep a disease from ever occurring — primary prevention. Secondary prevention would be finding a problem early, such as testing a provider after a needle stick. Tertiary prevention is treatment and rehabilitation after a disease has already caused harm. Quality control concerns reviewing care that was given, not preventing disease.
questions.question: Federal OSHA rules require your agency to offer every new EMT the hepatitis B vaccine series, free, within her first days in a job where she can be exposed to patients' blood — so her body builds its protection before the virus ever gets a chance. questions.explanation: What a course must teach and what a provider may do are two different questions with two different documents. The Education Standards answer the dean's first question — course content. The Scope of Practice Model answers the second, because it is the document that assigns skills to each provider level. A local protocol book only reflects one agency's rules inside that scope, and the Americans With Disabilities Act covers disability rights, not clinical skills.

questions.explanation: Quality control is oversight of the care given on individual calls: the medical director reviews a specific provider's reports, checks them against the standard, and corrects that provider. Continuous quality improvement — the label he used — is the system-wide side, collecting data from all crews over time to improve the whole system. Nothing in his description compares the agency with outside systems (benchmarking) or verifies a provider's qualifications to practice (credentialing).

questions.explanation: Endotracheal intubation, IV cardiac pharmacology, and rhythm interpretation together are the paramedic's advanced life support skill set — no lower level carries all three, which is why the intercept has to bring that level to the patient. An emergency medical responder provides basic first-response care only. The medical director and the emergency medical dispatcher direct care from off scene; neither rides the intercept to perform these skills.
